title: Quarterly Activities and Cashflow Report
body: Exmoor Minerals (ASX:EXM) provides its quarterly activities report for the period. Cash at bank was $4.2 million at quarter end. Exploration expenditure of $0.9 million was incurred at the Corella Well project, with assay results from the recent RC drilling program pending. Administrative costs remained in line with budget.

title: High-Grade Copper Intercepts at Corella Well
body: Exmoor Minerals is pleased to report assay results from the Stage 2 RC drilling program at the Corella Well project. Results include 18m at 2.4% Cu from 62m, including 6m at 4.1% Cu, and 11m at 1.9% Cu from 88m. These results extend the known mineralisation 200m along strike. Follow-up diamond drilling is planned for the next quarter.

title: Placement to Raise $6.5 Million and Share Purchase Plan
body: Exmoor Minerals has received firm commitments for a placement to sophisticated and institutional investors to raise approximately $6.5 million at $0.24 per share. The Company will also offer eligible shareholders the opportunity to participate in a Share Purchase Plan on the same terms, to raise up to a further $1.5 million. Funds raised will be used to accelerate follow-up drilling at Corella Well and for general working capital.

title: Investor Webinar: Corella Well Drilling Results and Capital Raise Briefing
body: Exmoor Minerals invites shareholders to an investor webinar hosted by Managing Director Sarah Kellerman, covering the recent Corella Well drilling results, the use of funds from the capital raise, and the outlook for the coming quarter. A recording will be made available on the investor hub for shareholders unable to attend live.

title: Quarterly Activities and Cashflow Report
body: Exmoor Minerals provides its quarterly activities report. Cash at bank was $9.8 million following completion of the placement and share purchase plan. Diamond drilling at Corella Well commenced during the quarter, with first assay results expected next quarter. The Company remains well funded to progress its exploration program.
